claims.statement: On the exact post-login Fedora 43 host, official Companion 4.3.3 image, and physical MK.2 serial A00SA5492OQMLF, the original SurfaceThread PID 73/startTicks 7808716 retained no current device descriptor for 30.483981415 seconds after the new USB epoch. One revalidated SIGTERM caused one replacement PID 858/startTicks 7817528 under the unchanged container and PID 1; the replacement acquired FD 20 on current inode 1480/rdev f1:0 and emitted ordered serial-specific Opening and Ready markers 1.137914595 and 1.138836576 seconds after signal receipt. The complete supported state was observed at 1.311634484 seconds.
claims.evidence: Canonical H-042 run and verification bound to image reference ghcr.io/bitfocus/companion/companion:v4.3.3, image ID sha256:2ff41215ab2ed77b5ec3dd74c5e6ec3b01354f57a7ca301b16017444d395544e, and evidence SHA-256 f4996a0d46c54fd337601e43ae7e0afa5e44d911c72c4888c0d1ae067fe0dc88.

claims.statement: The registered human authority @rodrigoteamx accepted the complete bounded H-042 motion on 2026-07-26, including preservation through a reviewed Git-tracked content-addressed bundle and local signed commits, while explicitly withholding authorization for push, merge, publication, release, installation, production signal policy, restart policy, or product-specification expansion.
claims.evidence: Human Doctrine review response 'Acepto la moción completa.' on 2026-07-26, anchored by the signed local governance acceptance commit containing this successor record.

claims.statement: The minimum replay closure contains 70 files and is preserved as a deterministic 290821-byte Git-tracked archive after a bounded disclosure scan found no credentials, tokens, passwords, cookies, private keys, email addresses, or MAC addresses.

Within only the exact tested H-042 boundary, SurfaceThread is the minimum observed replaceable unit that restored current-epoch MK.2 descriptor ownership and serial-specific Opening and Ready markers after automatic reacquisition remained negative; this orders the next investigation toward a safe recovery controller before any top-level container restart mechanism.
claims.evidence: Human-accepted bounded inference from canonical H-042 evidence f4996a0d46c54fd337601e43ae7e0afa5e44d911c72c4888c0d1ae067fe0dc88 and ADR-0006.

claims.statement: No accepted evidence yet establishes a safe production trigger, PID-reuse and race handling, acceptable downtime, security properties, repetition rate, long-outage behavior, multi-device behavior, pre-login behavior, or reboot recovery for worker replacement.
claims.evidence: Explicit H-042 claim exclusions and the accepted human motion; these questions require a successor governed Slice.

claims.statement: H-042 does not establish physical button command delivery, OverlayKit configuration continuity, rendered pixels, operator perception, OBS truth, or complete production recovery and does not alter SPEC-0001 or SPEC-0002.
claims.evidence: Canonical H-042 claimBoundary.excludes, accepted SPEC-0001 and SPEC-0002, and the human acceptance boundary.

claims.statement: The raw replay archive contains publication-sensitive local paths, host and Docker identifiers, hardware serials, group membership, and machine inventory; publication remains unauthorized and requires a separate disclosure decision.
claims.evidence: Bounded H-042 archive disclosure review on 2026-07-26 and the explicit no-push/no-publication human acceptance boundary.
